2011_015_011811org_regmtg.paragraph: Board packet for the Troy School District (Oakland County, Michigan) Board of Education's January 18, 2011 Organizational and Regular Meetings, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. The organizational half elects officers for terms until December 31, 2011, appoints Assistant Superintendent for Business Services Mark S. Rajter as Treasurer, and adopts a depository and investment resolution naming nine banks and twelve investment institutions. The regular half carries the November and December 2010 Treasurer's Reports and check registers, Schools of Choice resolutions for 2011-2012, bid awards to Edline ($29,436.00) and Paetec-Tampa ($59,118.55), and an agreement to sell Troy administrative consulting services to Avondale School District for fees not exceeding $200,000.00 annually.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education, Organizational Meeting followed by Regular Meeting, January 18, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) per the organizational agenda, Channel 58 (Comcast) per the regular agenda.

**Organizational actions**
Judy Brill is appointed temporary secretary; president, vice president and secretary are elected for terms until December 31, 2011, roll calls listing Philippart, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff and Miletti. Mark S. Rajter is appointed Treasurer for January through December 2011. The depository resolution names Bank of America, Bank of New York, Charter One, Chase, Comerica, Fifth Third, MILAF, PFM Securities through Fifth Third and PNC Bank, plus twelve investment institutions; investments follow Board Policy D-1103 and Section 380.1223(1)(h) of the Revised School Code, and health/dependent care checks over $10,000 need the added signature of Jasen Witt or Monica Papasian. The Superintendent continues as Deputy Secretary, Judy Brill posts meeting notices, and the 2011 calendar is adopted, with workshops at 6:00 p.m. at 4400 Livernois, a Board Winter Retreat January 21, 2011, and the June 7 Annual Recognition Meeting at Athens High School.

**Consent agenda**
December 6, 2010 special meeting minutes (Resolutions 10-118 through 10-122, each Ayes 7 / Nays 0, including a cardio equipment award to All Pro Exercise of $11,999.50 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund; closed session 7:15 p.m. to 8:25 p.m.; adjournment 8:26 p.m.), December 14, 2010 workshop minutes (Schools of Choice projections; 2011/2012 budget assumptions), and the November and December 2010 Treasurer's Reports.

**Budget reports (General Fund: 101, 120, 122, 129, 140)**
Both year-to-date statements print an original revenue budget of $134,308,608 against expenditures of $135,793,505, excess revenue over expenditures of ($1,484,897), and fund balance of $18,120,438 at July 1, 2010 and $16,635,541 at June 30, 2011. Revenue actual is $36,572,408 at November and $46,795,189 at December; expenditure actual is $40,610,764 at November and $51,691,924 at December, with $64,279,024 encumbered and $19,822,557 (14.60%) available. A Special Revenue footnote records that the fund balance on the budget resolution was $7,639,053 because it included $5,610,166 of Durant fund balance that beginning 2010-2011 is part of the General Fund.

**Curriculum, business and other**
Resolutions adopt limited Schools of Choice programs under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, for nonresident kindergarten and first-grade students in 2011-2012. A report covers Troy High School's selection as one of four national teams in NASA's DIME competition, traveling to Glenn Research Center March 21-25, 2011. Business items award web hosting to Edline for $29,436.00 (Bid 9701) and PRI local/long distance service to Paetec-Tampa for $59,118.55 (Bid 9699), and authorize the Avondale School District administrative services agreement. Other items approve Ms. Philippart's attendance at the NSBA Federal Relations Network Conference in Washington, D.C., February 6-8, 2011, and schedule a special meeting for January 25, 2011 on the vacancy created by Carol Pochodylo's resignation.

**Identification.** Troy School District (Oakland County, Michigan) Board of Education packet for the Organizational Meeting and Regular Meeting of January 18, 2011, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; administrative address 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) per the organizational agenda, Channel 58 (Comcast) per the regular agenda, and Channel 15 (WOW) on both.

**Organizational meeting.** The Board elects an acting chairperson, who appoints Judy Brill temporary secretary, then elects a president, vice president and secretary each "until December 31, 2011"; roll calls list Philippart, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff and Miletti. Item 6.B appoints Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, as Treasurer for January through December 2011. Item 6.C adopts the Fund Depositories and Investment Resolution for the same period, naming nine depositories — Bank of America, Bank of New York, Charter One Bank, Chase Bank, Comerica Bank, Fifth Third Bank, MILAF, PFM Securities, Inc. through Fifth Third Bank, and PNC Bank — and twelve investment institutions, adding Ambassador Capital Management, Citizens Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, Morgan Stanley Smith Barney and The Private Bank. Withdrawals carry Rajter's facsimile signature, with emergency handwritten signature by the Treasurer or Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler on the General Fund and Payroll accounts at Bank of America; Troy Career Center checks at PNC Bank are signed by Dorothy Kaltz, Jennifer Llewellyn, Kathy Molesa or Lyda Keough; health and dependent care claim checks over $10,000 require the added signature of Jasen Witt or Finance Director Monica Papasian. Funds are invested under Board Policy D-1103 and subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code; the certification is dated the 18th day of January 2011. Item 6.D continues the Superintendent as Deputy Secretary for the 2011 calendar year, 6.E designates Judy Brill, Secretary to the Superintendent, to post notices, and 6.F adopts the 2011 calendar of regular meetings at the Services Building at 7:00 p.m. and workshops at 6:00 p.m. at 4400 Livernois, including the January 21 Board Winter Retreat and the June 7 Annual Recognition Meeting at Athens High School.

**Recognition and minutes.** The regular agenda recognizes 72 Senior Scholar Athletes for 2010-11 at a 3.5 grade point average from Athens and Troy High Schools, plus ten Fall 2010 All-State athletes including Sean Cunningham, Jacob Duzey, Kelly Feng, Brett Forman, Monique Nguyen and Jennifer Yang. The December 6, 2010 special meeting, called to order at 7:00 p.m. by President Underwood with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart and Pochodylo present, adopted Resolutions 10-118 (November 16, 2010 minutes), 10-119 (new hire Jennifer Liwienski), 10-120 (cardio equipment bid to All Pro Exercise, $11,999.50, from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund), 10-121 (cancelling the December 14, 2010 meeting) and 10-122 (closed session on negotiations), each Ayes 7, Nays 0; closed session ran 7:15 p.m. to 8:25 p.m. and adjournment was at 8:26 p.m., signed Nancy L. Philippart, Secretary. The December 14, 2010 workshop ran 6:05 p.m. to 7:32 p.m. on Schools of Choice projections and 2011/2012 budget assumptions.

**Treasurer's Reports.** Rajter's November memo (dated December 8, 2010, Business Department, 4400 Livernois, 248-823-4022) lists disbursements by fund of General Fund $2,421,814.33, Grant Fund $18,667.04, Troy Career Center $28,547.57, Durant Fund zero, Community Education $16,723.94 and Food Service $4,427.61, and summary lines of Total General Fund $2,469,028.94, Total Special Revenue Funds $21,151.55, Debt Funds $15,258.07, Building & Site Funds $322,167.52, Student Activity Fund $114,620.14, ACH debits $14,659.92, outgoing wire transfers $1,266,816.91, Total Disbursements in Period $4,223,703.05, and prior period voids of $2,347.00 (checks 289487 for 2,288.00 and 289634 for 59.00). The December memo (dated January 7, 2011) lists General Fund $1,325,160.93, Grant Fund $13,071.47, Troy Career Center $13,466.14, Community Education $13,588.85 and Food Service $11,452.18, and Total General Fund $1,351,698.54, Total Special Revenue Funds $25,041.03, Debt Funds $1,891.82, Building & Site Funds $165,129.75, Student Activity Fund $94,349.70, Memorial Scholarship Fund $400.00, ACH debits $41,359.66, outgoing wire transfers $2,150,390.85, Total Disbursements in Period $3,830,261.35, and prior period voids of $1,918.75 (checks 286422 $73.00, 289877 $1,702.00, 290176 $106.75, 290203 $60.00, 290261 $50.00).

**Check registers.** Both registers are Pentamation Enterprises, Inc. report ACCTPA21, "Check Register - By Fund," with every line posting to cash account A1003 at zero sales tax. The November register (printed 12/07/2010, accounting period 6/11) totals 2,942,226.22, with fund totals of 2,193,499.04 (101 General), 18,667.04 (120 Grant), 228,315.29 (122 Special Ed), 28,547.57 (129 TCC Grant), 10,553.15 (304), 3,701.43 (306), 1,003.49 (307), 322,167.52 (404 Capital Project), 4,427.61 (520 Food Service), 16,723.94 (530 Continuing Education), 111,990.28 (700 Student Activity) and 2,629.86 (701). The December register (printed 01/07/2011, period 7/11) totals 1,638,510.84, with 101 at 1,147,759.88, 120 at 13,071.47, 122 at 177,401.05, 129 at 13,466.14, 304 at 1,308.46, 306 at 458.94, 307 at 124.42, 404 at 165,129.75, 520 at 11,452.18, 530 at 13,588.85, 700 at 93,935.14, 701 at 414.56 and 750 Memorial Scholarship at 400.00. Notable payments include check 290258 to MI EDUC SPEC SERV A for December 2010 premiums of 1,147,902.24 plus COBRA of 2,559.56 (total 1,150,461.80); Blue Care Network 64,987.11; Enviro Clean Services checks of 267,428.76, 215,656.04 and 81,502.99, with custodian service lines of 208,118.13 and 208,118.10; First Group America 166,048.73 and 157,762.31 for general-education routes and 147,167.64 and 143,969.76 in the Special Ed Fund; Integrys Energy Services 72,122.09; R K A Petroleum 29,690.63; Royal Oak School District tuition 28,365.00; NETECH Corp 40,963.00; Plante & Moran audit services 19,500.00; Clark Hill PLC legal 8,523.00; Oakland County Treasurer tax settlements netting 66,995.66 and 8,306.71; Peterson Glass exterior doors 71,370.00 and 103,971.00; General Sports Venue synthetic turf 97,765.20. Board items include seven $50.00 "1ST BD PMT 2010" payments to Ida Edmunds, Paula Fleming, Gary Hauff, Todd Miletti, Nancy Philippart, Carol Pochodylo and Wendy Underwood, Philippart's MASB conference 193.90, and board member name badges 66.00. November wires include MPSERS of -2,223,383.03; December wires include a VRIP payment of -85,437.60.

**Budget statements.** The November and December year-to-date Summary Revenue and Expense Budget Reports for fiscal year 2011 cover the General Fund (101, 120, 122, 129, 140), Special Revenue (520, 530), Debt Service (394, 397, 304, 306), Capital Projects (404) and Internal Service (681). General Fund original budgets are $134,308,608 revenue and $135,793,505 expenditures; revenue actual is $36,572,408 (72.77% uncollected) at November and $46,795,189 (65.16%) at December, while expenditure actual is $40,610,764 at November and $51,691,924 at December with $64,279,024 encumbered and $19,822,557 available (14.60%). Both statements show excess revenue over expenditures of ($1,484,897) and fund balance of $18,120,438 at July 1, 2010 and $16,635,541 at June 30, 2011. Consolidated Special Revenue shows $5,145,806 budgeted revenue against $2,407,308 actual in December, expenditures of $5,445,677 against $991,622, an excess of ($299,871), and fund balance from $2,028,887 to $1,729,016, footnoted that the budget-resolution balance of $7,639,053 included $5,610,166 of Durant fund balance now part of the General Fund; Food Service moves from $925,233 to $837,024 and Adult & Community Education from $1,103,654 to $891,992. Debt Service budgets $18,761,527 in property taxes ($9,700,072 collected by December), $11,925,000 in principal redemption with no actual and $6,350,200 in interest with $3,175,100 paid, an excess of $326,027, and fund balance from $946,534 to $1,272,561. Capital Projects budgets $7,216,120 in expenditures against $3,465,605 actual at December, an excess of ($7,156,120), and fund balance from $8,441,765 to $1,285,645. The Internal Service Fund carries a $120,000 VRIP expense line and fund balance of $33,531 unchanged.

**Curriculum items.** Resolutions 7.A and 7.B adopt limited Schools of Choice programs for the 2011-2012 school year for nonresident kindergarten and first-grade students under Section 105 (within Oakland County) and Section 105c (districts in another county whose intermediate school district is contiguous with Oakland ISD) of the State School Aid Act of 1979, as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996. Item 7.C reports Troy High School's team as one of four proposals selected nationally in NASA's DIME (Dropping In a Microgravity Environment) competition, traveling March 21-25, 2011 to NASA's Glenn Research Center in Cleveland, Ohio for the 2.2-second drop tower; teacher John Morrison, Science Coordinator Jennifer Gottlieb and students Sara Guenther, Nicholas Krajewski, Mason Liang and Mihir Pande presented "Effect of Microgravity on the Motion of Air Bubbles in Water."

**Business items.** Item 8.A authorizes an Agreement for Administrative Services Consultants with Avondale School District, 2940 Waukegan Street, Auburn Hills, Michigan 48326, effective July 1, 2010 through June 30, 2011 with annual renewal options, citing Sections 11a(3) and (4) of the School Code, MCL 380.1 et seq. Named consultants are Jasen Witt (human resources), Mark Rajter and Frank Lams (business management, approximately 40% FTE) and Dominick Asaro (transportation, approximately 50% FTE); total fees "shall not exceed two hundred thousand and 00/100 Dollars ($200,000.00) annually," and invoices are submitted on or before January 1 and June 30 with payment by February 1 and August 1. Termination requires sixty days' notice or a thirty-day cure; records follow Bulletin 522 and FERPA; background checks follow Public Act 680 of 2006 with reporting under MCL 380.1535a(1) and 380.1539b(1); venue is Oakland County. Exhibits list bargaining units (Teachers, Secretaries, Para-Educators and Alternative Education Teachers under MEA; Transportation under AFSCME) with Bonnie Lobert, reporting duties covering the FID, SE-4096, SE-4094, SE-4107, USF, FS-4731, SM-4012 and L-4029 reports under supervisor Frank E. Lams with Monica Papasian and Renelle Tolan, and routing coordinator Suzanne Oselett. Item 8.B awards Bid 9701 for web hosting service to Edline for $29,436.00 after four compliant bids were opened January 5, 2011 on a bid released November 11, 2010; Director of Technology Scott Bryan cites an estimated 38% E-Rate discount, rejects THiNQ Ed for incompatibility with GradeQuick Web, and recommends a one-year contract commencing July 1, 2011 (the resolution names the 2010/11 General Fund while Frank E. Lams' memo names 2011/12). Item 8.C awards Bid 9699 for PRI local and long distance service to Paetec-Tampa at $59,118.55 as an expenditure of the 2011/12, 2012/13 and 2013/14 General Funds; the evaluation used October 2010 volumes of 4 PRI circuits, 2,700 DID numbers and 8,677 calls, projecting monthly costs of $1,642 for Paetec Tampa, $1,947 for Telnet Worldwide, $2,437 for Cavalier measured rate and $2,446 for Cavalier flat rate, with 36-month totals of $59,118.55, $70,089.91, $87,725.75 and $88,069.01; the PAETEC Fairport, New York bid was rejected.

**Other and closed session.** Item 10.A, citing Board Policy B-2001, approves Board Secretary Ms. Philippart's attendance at the National School Boards Association Annual Federal Relations Network Conference in Washington, D.C., February 6-8, 2011, noting Troy was one of six districts selected by the Oakland County School Board Association for a $500 scholarship. Item 10.B schedules a Special Board of Education Meeting for Tuesday, January 25, 2011 at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building for candidates for the vacancy created by Carol Pochodylo's resignation. Item 11.A resolves to enter closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), with a roll call listing Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Underwood and Edmunds.
